utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, can you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case Number IT-01-47-T, The Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam Registrar. Appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, counsel. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis, Ekkehard Withopf, and Ruth Karper, the case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Withopf. Appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of General Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, counsel, Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel, and Muriel Cauvin, legal assistant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Mr. Mulalic, legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Chamber would like to greet everybody present in the courtroom, representatives of the Prosecution, representatives of the Defence, the accused, as well as the accused, as well as the court reporter, who is taking notes today, as well as the representative of the Registry. In order for us to be able to follow today's hearing, we have to say that we shall continue the cross-examination of the witness whom we heard yesterday. Therefore, I'm going to ask the usher to bring the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We continue your testimony today. I'm going to give the floor to the Defence for the questions within the scope of their cross-examination. The Defence has the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, we spoke about numerous problems in detecting and prosecution of perpetrators of crimes and efforts undertaken by the law enforcement agency in order to elucidate crimes and punish the perpetrators thereof. Is it true, Mr. Kapetanovic, that in some cases you managed to detect the perpetrator of the crime immediately and undertake prosecution measures immediately? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In response to that question, I would like to mention some specific events and specific perpetrators. It's very hard to say whether we did or whether we did not. But there were such cases despite the difficulties that we spoke about yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask the usher to present to the witness a number of indictments that the Defence managed to come across during their investigation in the court in Zenica. This is going to serve to corroborate what the witness has just said in response to my previous answer. Mr. Kapetanovic, we have photocopied just the introduction into the indictment. We have omitted the statement of reasons that is contained in every indictment. Is this an indictment brought by the court where you served as the prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I don't remember. I'm looking at the indictment. I'm looking at the name. I have looked at the factual description of the crime, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It may have been our mistake not to have given you the entire indictment. However, this is one of the indictments where the incident and the indictment were made at the same time. Have there been cases that because of the problems with the detection of crimes, the prosecution did not take place at the same time because it was necessary to verify facts about the crime and the perpetrator thereof? Was that another situation that you faced during that year?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please explain a little bit what you're aiming at? I did not quite understand your question. Your question was rather broad.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the first case, that's what I've asked you, due to the difficulties that you had in detecting and prosecution, and according to the report there were hundreds of perpetrators at that time, is it true that in some situations like the first one that I showed to you, you were able to detect the perpetrator immediately and immediately prosecute such a perpetrator?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are still not able to do that, and especially this was not possible during that period of time. This was a specific time, if we are talking about the years 1993 and 1994. So it was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, if the law enforcement agency were to detect a perpetrator immediately, then a procedure before the high court in Zenica was instigated immediately.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the perpetrator was detected and, especially if he was involved in a grave crime, then this incident would be given a lot more attention than a misdemeanor or an offence carrying a lower penalty. And the police as law enforcement agency took statements, collected evidence, both objective and subjective evidence and then they file a report to the criminal prosecutor's office. In more serious cases, this was done in cooperation with the prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In such situation when the perpetrator was discovered and if that perpetrator had committed a serious crime, it was customary and even obligatory to remand such a perpetrator in custody. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, I'm going to show you an example from your prosecutor's office to illustrate what we have just been talking about. This is one of the examples from the prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the usher please show the document to the witness. We have enough copies for the Honourable Judges and all the others present in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Just for the record, I'm not sure what my learned colleague is intending on doing with the previous document. But just so as to avoid confusion, perhaps it either should be withdrawn or marked for identification so that we don't have numerous documents floating around without numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. As regards the first document, indictment brought against Mr. Atif Karic, what is your intention? Do you want to tender this document into evidence or did you just produce this document for the purpose of your cross-examination without the intention of tendering it into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would first like this document to be marked for identification. This is one of the documents we found in the archives. Since the witness could not remember this document, I would not tender it into admission of evidence, but I would like it to be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are going to give a number to this document to be marked for identification, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: DH57 and DH57/E, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document has been marked for identification. DH57, B/C/S version, and DH57/E, English translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The second document I have given to the witness, can it be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document concerning Osman Buhic, Madam Registrar, can you please give us a number for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: DH58 and DH58/E, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. DH58, B/C/S; DH58/E, English translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, is this a request to carry out an investigation, the number is KT3873, dated 31st of August 1993. This was filed against three persons who were immediately remanded in custody because there was a suspicion that they had committed an aggravated robbery. Is that one of the documents that we spoke about just a little while ago?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you will allow me, I would like to draw a parallel between the first document and this one. Yesterday, I told you that I was very busy. I did not participate in the cases because I had a number of deputies at that time. One of my deputies was Obrad Rajcevic, which I apologise if I didn't mention him yesterday when I was giving you the name of my deputies. And as far as your question is concerned, and this particular case, this indeed was a very serious crime. Those persons were in uniforms, and they misrepresented themselves as members of the army. They were remanded in custody. What else could a prosecutor do? This was a very difficult and critical year, and the person who was attacked was of a different ethnic background. Nothing else could be done but what was indeed done and what was described here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since the witness has identified the document and also recognised his deputy who drafted this document, I would like to tender this document into evidence in order to prove that the prosecutor prosecuted such crimes, qualified such crimes, and that those crimes were tried in keeping with the law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution has no objection to this document being admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, are you going to give us a number, and are you going to render your ruling on the admission of this document into evidence, or shall I proceed with my cross-examination before that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed. You have two other documents, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, in order to show the Trial Chamber an example of what you just spoken about, I would like to ask you, is it correct that some crimes, even serious crimes, despite all the efforts invested by the law enforcement agencies and the prosecutor have never been elucidated, and the perpetrators have never been discovered? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please show a document to the witness, an investigation started in January 1993. However, the perpetrator was not discovered even up to the year 2003.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: For clarification, the Defence found these documents during their investigation in the archives of the cantonal court and the cantonal prosecutor's office in Zenica. For the purpose of this cross-examination, only the first and the last documents were taken. However, we have a lot more documents illustrating efforts invested at that time by the law enforcement agencies and by the prosecutor's office. And while the witness is looking at this document, I would kindly ask for these two documents to be given a number for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we have the first document. The date is 20 May 2003. The document was signed by Mr. Curic, who is the deputy prosecutor. Mr. Mundis, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the record, the Prosecution would object to my learned colleague's characterisation or statement that they have numerous documents in their possession. The Prosecution submits that that borders on testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber has noted that the Defence has a number of documents, but are only presenting a few. They are not going to introduce other documents. We shall rely on the documents that are discussed today, not on the whole number of documents. The documents signed by the deputy cantonal prosecutor, Mr. Curic, the date is 20 May 2003. Madam Registrar, can we please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: DH59 and DH59/E, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] DH59 in B/C/S; DH59/E, English. And we have a second document. The date is 2nd February 1993 signed by a judge, Mr. Faik Spahic. This document should also be marked for identification. Madam Registrar, can we have a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: DH60 and DH60/E marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] DH60 for B/C/S; DH60/E, English version. Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, if you look at the document with the date 26 January 1996 [as interpreted], is this a record of the on-site investigation into the murder of Bruno Skocilic?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have looked at the record. I have looked at the decision. I remember the case because the father of the victim came to see me on a number of occasions. This incident was before my term of office. I started my term of office on the 20th of May of that year. This is not important. I'm just mentioning it -- this. You've asked me whether there were such cases. Yes, there were such cases, and this incident also is one of those where the perpetrator was not found, although we had a desire to elucidate this event because of the -- event because of the family and because of the fact that this young man, as far as I can remember, was a member of the army or the police. Either of the army or of the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So you confirm that you are aware of this case, that it was prosecuted by your prosecutor's office, that despite all the efforts and investigation, the perpetrator was never discovered up to the year 2003?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that. And we are still investigating this crime together with a number of other crimes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. My colleague has an objection to raise, it seems.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, actually page 9, line 11 in the English transcript, the date of the document says 1996. And in fact, the date of the document is 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's the 22 -- no, the date on the document is the 26th of January 1993. It's not 1996. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I suggest that both documents that have been recognised by the Prosecution as documents from the archives of the high court in Zenica and the victim of the murder, Bruno Skocilic, has also been recognised, as well as his father. As a result, I think we have all the elements we need for these two documents to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll turn to the Prosecution. I would like to point out that the Defence is requesting that four documents be admitted into evidence. These are official documents. They're all from the prosecutor's office in Zenica. The witness has recognised the documents, and the documents deal with investigations conducted during the period when the witness held his post as a judge. As far as the last document is concerned, he wasn't holding his position, but as he took office in May, he was competent because his position included -- covered the investigation that was still ongoing. And this investigation wasn't concluded because the perpetrators weren't identified. The witness has identified these documents which relate to the duties that he performed. The Defence has pointed out that crimes were committed apparently by individuals who claimed to be members of the military. What is the Prosecution's position in relation to the admissibility into evidence of these documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution has no objection to DH59 and DH60 being admitted into evidence. Again, I would note page 10, line 14 of the English transcript indicates the documents have been recognised by the Prosecution. That should be "recognised by the witness."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The documents were recognised by the witness who worked as a prosecutor at the time. After the break, we will render a decision about these four documents, two of which haven't been objected to.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, yesterday, my learned colleague from the Prosecution asked you a number of questions that concerned the information you had about people who had been taken to the hospital in Zenica from the Susanj and Ovnak area. They had been taken to the mortuary in June 1993. Although these factors aren't contained in the indictment, I have a few questions that I would like to ask you in relation to what the Prosecution asked you about. Before I do so, I would like to point out, Your Honours, that in the course of its investigations, Defence counsel found some of the documents in the archives of the cantonal court in Zenica. They concern this period, and they found some documents from the prosecutor's office in Zenica. Before questions are put to the witness, I would like these documents to be shown to the witness. We have a sufficient number of copies for the Trial Chamber and for our colleagues in the courtroom. I would also like to say that from that documents from the prosecutor's office, we've changed a document, which is the official note of Vlado Adamovic. We have exchanged it with an identical document provided to us by the Prosecutor's office because that document has a Prosecution title, and it's already been translated into English. We wanted to use that document and not the one that was in the archives. And I would like to reiterate that the document is identical; the only difference is that it bears a Prosecution number. As the witness has had a look at the document, I would like to ask the witness to answer a number of questions. It's true that over ten years have passed since the event. The Trial Chamber has pointed this out on a number of occasions. And with regard to this subject, Mr. Kapetanovic, would it be true to say that certain rumours and information were obtained by you unofficially, at least initially? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the 17 corpses that were taken to the mortuary -- well, I don't remember having mentioned rumours. But perhaps I made -- perhaps I heard rumours, too, and my colleague, Suada Halilagic, told me something about that. She had more information about that than I did, at least as far as I can remember. Vlado Adamovic, the judge, told her about this. He is the person who compiled the official note. So I am telling you what I can remember from that period. I'd like to repeat that she arranged a meeting, and I remember that it was after 10 or 15 days at the most. That's when we spoke to Mr. Ramiz Dugalic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the documents that we found in the course of our investigation, there's a document, number KT9793, dated the 5th of October 1993 which your colleague forwarded to the district military court, to the judge, Vlado Adamovic. In that document, she requests that the judge provide his own information about this event. Is it possible that your prosecution wanted to participate in clarifying the circumstances and also to see what jurisdiction it had to deal with the particular case? Was that the purpose of the document -- of the request?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stand by everything that I said yesterday about this event. And I wouldn't want to repeat anything. But the question you're asking me, as to whether it was our desire, well, yes, absolutely it was. That is why we went to discuss this matter, that apart from the fact that it's my duty to tell the truth and nothing but the truth, I would also like to show that my intentions are good. Believe it or not, what you have now shown to me, KTI97/93, dated the 5th of October 1993, this is a document that my colleague, Suada Halilagic, compiled on her own initiative. I haven't seen such a document before. Perhaps I saw it, but I don't remember. But I would like to repeat that I don't know the reasons for which my colleague compiled this document on her own initiative. And if you will allow me to comment, I don't see that she erred in compiling this document. She showed her goodwill in clarifying the matter. Whether -- the body she wanted to do this with is not important, what is important is she wanted to discover the perpetrator.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, I wasn't suggesting that something wrong had been done here. The procedure followed seems to be quite legal. Is it correct to say that this document, which is in the archives of the court and of your office, on the same date at the request of your colleague, the judge from the military court responded to the document and attached documents, his own official note and information that he provided to the executive committee of the assembly of Zenica Municipality?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With regard to this document and my colleague's request, I have nothing that I'd like to repeat. As far as the official note is concerned, I told the investigator when he was in Zenica that a record was made, and my colleague Vlado Adamovic went to the site. And when the investigator showed me the record, I read it. And I remember, in spite of the fact that I have the document before me now, that an official note was made. And it was on the basis of the fact that some individuals had recognised the corpses.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the note compiled by your colleague, Mr. Adamovic, which you were familiar with then as you are now, did not show the crimes had been committed against these persons. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to see Mr. Dugalic for the sake of caution to check up on this, to make sure that I hadn't made an error. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So Mr. Kapetanovic, could I draw the conclusion that in addition to those efforts, communication with the court, with the security organ of the 3rd Corps, in 1993, you didn't obtain any information that would support the suspicion that a crime had been committed?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. And the reason is as follows: I thought in each case that this was a matter for the military prosecutor's office or the court or the military police to deal with. And I have spoken about this -- I spoke about this yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that after the Dayton Agreement was signed and peace was established in Bosnia-Herzegovina, prosecution offices in Herceg-Bosna and the prosecution in the part of the state that was under the control of the BH army exchanged information on many events that transpired in the course of the war?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is absolutely correct. But if you have any specific cases you would like to mention, I might be able to remember them. As far as I can remember, that was an exchange that had to do with court decisions in 1996, perhaps a little later too.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that immediately after the war, a large number of indictments appeared, were issued, and there were investigations into scores, sometimes hundreds of individuals. And as a result, the international community had to respond to this. And with the cooperation of the ICTY, it had to adopt the so-called "rules of the road." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the sake of caution, I just want to be brief. Bosniaks fled in one direction; Croats in other. The HVO, their bodies, took statements from Croatian victims, and we took statements from Bosniaks. So we had proof about crimes committed by HVO members and they allegedly had proof of crimes committed by the army. When this exchange took place, I remember very well that in one request for an investigation and in a decision on conducting an investigation, we were provided with cases concerning 55 persons. Spahic Besim, and I think I can say he wouldn't even kill an ant. I was surprised to see they had submitted these cases to the Tribunal so they could assess it. And the Tribunal, and this also has to do with the music school, the Tribunal pronounced itself on about four or five individuals. I think they -- I think I could remember certain names and numbers in relation to category A. I don't know if this answer is sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution would like to briefly address the Trial Chamber in private session, if that's possible, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go into private session, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now that we are in open session, Defence counsel has requested that a number of documents be tendered into evidence. The Prosecution has no objection with regard to DH58, 59, and 60. With regard to DH57 marked for identification, the Prosecution is not under the impression that the Defence wants to tender this document into evidence. And as far as the subject of the 17 victims is concerned that were carried out by the witness's deputy, the Defence is requesting that this document be tendered into evidence. So what is the Prosecution's position with regard to having these documents tendered into evidence, the documents which come from Suada Halilagic and the competent military court, as well as documents that have to do with autopsies?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could just get a clarification from my learned colleague, is she intending to tender this entire case file as one exhibit? Is that the intention of the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I assume from the Registrar this would be DH61?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no objection to DH61 being admitted into evidence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Mundis. We will withdraw now to have our break. And we will render our decision at 10 to 11.00, after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll now resume and the Trial Chamber will render its decision regarding the documents. The bundle that was just presented, the number that will be given is 61. DH61, B/C/S, DH61/E will be the number for the English translation. We also admit into evidence DH60, DH59, and DH58. DH57 which is a document which hasn't been recognised by the witness will not be admitted. That deals with the documents. Madam Registrar, we will now go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in open session. You may proceed with your questions, and the Trial Chamber will also ask the witness some questions, if the questions that you have don't relate to the questions that the Trial Chamber would like to ask the witness, which concern certain legal, technical matters. You may take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday, you discussed the problems that the high prosecutor's office had working in 1993 and 1994.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday, I spoke not only about the problems in the prosecutor's office, but also about judicial problems in general. I was also referring to the military prosecutor's office, to the military court and to the cantonal, that is to say, the high court during the relevant period. And naturally, to my own office. It was extremely difficult to work at the time. The judicial system was functioning. We did perform our duties, but the borders were closed off. We were under a blockade. There was a shortage of everything, paper, water, electricity. I'm referring to this particular period of time. And we were only able to function thanks to the BH Army at the time. This enabled us to function to a certain extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Another particular problem was collecting evidence and finding witnesses who weren't in Zenica or who were in the territory under the control of the HVO. And it was then difficult to process certain cases immediately. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's absolutely correct. If you need certain clarifications, I can go into that. If not, please tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that representatives of the prosecution, the civilian police, and the military police weren't able to perform any duties in the territory under the control of the HVO? They weren't able to collect evidence?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During this period of time, it was impossible to establish contact of any sort, especially if it concerned crimes or if it related to Chapter 16, that is to say, crimes against humanity and international law. In spite of the fact that we knew each other very well before the war, both sides knew each other very well before the war, but in spite of this fact it was difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, in response to a question from Ms. Residovic, you said if you had left, perhaps you wouldn't have returned.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said. And I was referring to that period, and I stand by what I said. I know what the situation was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you think that you might have been arrested or detained at that time?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. All I can say is that I doubt that I would have returned had I left. But as to what would have happened to me, I don't know. I'm again referring to that period in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When an agreement was reached about an exchange of information between the courts, the prosecutor's offices and the competent organs, the prosecutor's office was able to process cases far more efficiently because all the evidence and relevant facts were at his disposal. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. It wasn't an exchange of information; it was an exchange of documents. Prosecution documents and court documents. But the documents that we received which had to do with war crimes, we would supplement them. I could provide you with an example; when I say that we supplemented this evidence and asking for further clarifications, we even interviewed the same witnesses who had been interviewed by HVO representatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: One of the cases that you mentioned a while ago and after agreement had been reached on carrying out a case, it concerned the music school. It was a request for investigating Isic Jasmin, a person whose name has been mentioned quite frequently here. It also concerned certain other individuals. And you personally submitted a request for carrying out an investigation to the competent court in Zenica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, among those 55 cases, 55 individuals I have mentioned today whom we had brought from the district military court in Travnik, this trial provided evidence and Isic was categorised under A and the two Osmanovic brothers and someone called Karamuja Vehid. I didn't instigate any proceedings with regard to this individual, though I can clarify why.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown document from the cantonal prosecutor's office in Zenica that he himself compiled. It's a request for conducting an investigation into these persons, and the period is 1993. And it also concerns a war crime against the civilian population and prisoners. We have a sufficient number of copies for everyone in the courtroom, and we have informed the Prosecution of this document before the hearing today.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, did you draft this document, the request for investigation?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date is 5 November 2001. I drafted it myself, and I'm in charge of this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has recognised the document. He drafted it himself. The Defence believes that this document is very relevant for this procedure and tenders this document into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may ask your question to the witness based on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Having filed this request for investigation to the competent court, the investigating judge of the cantonal court in Zenica issued a decision on investigation to be carried out. The investigation was carried out in order to investigate war crimes against the civilian population. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. But an addition is in order if this is allowed. On the 1st of August 2003, a new Law on Criminal Procedure of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina came into effect, and this investigation was returned to the cantonal prosecutor's office in Zenica, and this investigation is now run by this prosecutor's office. As far as the brother Osmanovic and Isic, this is continued, and witnesses are being heard as mentioned in the preamble of this request for investigation. Dragan Janjic has been heard already, and he denied whatever he had already said to members of the HVO. Amongst other things, he says that this statement is not his, that the signature was not his. So we had to verify all these checks. We conducted an interview, and he said that he knew Karamuja, but that he had never touched him. That is exactly what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you, sir. With regard to other individuals which are indicated in the request for investigation, what is happening with the investigation?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigation is underway in the cantonal court in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the usher please now show another document to the witness. This is the decision on conducting the investigation pursuant to the request that was filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. First, we're going to render a decision on this document. This document was drafted by the prosecutor's office in Zenica and referred to the investigating judge. The request was for an investigation to be carried out with regard to the events that involved military policemen of the BiH Army. The period is between 19 April 1993 and the 5th of September of the same year. The witness has recognised the document. However, he has told us that after the amendments to the Law on Criminal Procedure, this investigation, as far as we understood the witness, was referred back to the prosecutor's office so the investigating judge was no longer in charge of this after the amendments to the Law on Criminal Procedure which took place on the 5th of November 2003. What can the Prosecutor tell us about the admissibility of this document into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution has no objection to this document being admitted into evidence. However, we would respectfully request that it be put under seal in light of the Chamber's ruling at the beginning of this session. There is reference in there to matters which were the subject of the Trial Chamber's ruling. But we have no objection to its admissibility. We will simply ask that it be admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please tell us what facts should be under seal? You're saying that this document is linked with what has been said previously. We are going to go into private session first. Madam Registrar, can you please make sure we are in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kapetanovic, yesterday in the course of the cross-examination, you mentioned reports that you submitted to the republican public prosecutor's office and to the civilian organs of power in 1993 and 1994. These reports concerned the work of the prosecutor's office. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I discussed this subject yesterday, and I stand by everything I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In order to clarify matters, I don't think it entered the transcript when you mentioned the reports that had to be submitted on behalf of the municipal prosecutor's offices in Travnik, Bugojno, and Zavidovici. You said that because it was difficult to establish contact, you couldn't obtain such reports.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's probably the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Were these simple communication problems or was it because of the total blockade and the impossibility of gaining access to reports from these prosecutors offices?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you tell me the date of the report?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: 25 February 1994.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite possible, that that was the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Kapetanovic. We have no further questions for this witness. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Trial Chamber has a few minor questions for you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the report that you forwarded to your superior that was presented yesterday, mention was made of the fact that a state of war was declared and you mentioned the Official Gazette in your report, and the number 7/92 was mentioned. Either that was July 1992 or it's number 7 in 1992. The declaration of a state of war, did this involve amendments in your texts as far as applicable law in a state of peace is concerned? Was the penal procedure changed as a result of the declaration of a state of war?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When a state of war is declared, everything is changed. Everything changed physically and in legal terms. There was confusion. People were mobilised, and then a number of decrees were issued. I can't remember which decrees were adopted at the moment. But in legal terms, there were very significant changes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And the date of the declaration of the state of war, can you remember it, or are you not able to remember it?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You said that there were two military courts, one of which was in Zenica. Where was the actual geographical location of this military court?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The cantonal, that is to say, the high court was located where it is located to this very day. As far as the military court is concerned, it was located about 200 metres as the crow flies from that court. It was located in the residential premises of a company that moved out. Those premises were empty. And when that military court was established, they moved into those facilities, both the military court and the district -- both the military court and the military prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In response to a question, you said that there were two military courts. There was the court in Zenica and there was another one in Travnik that you mentioned. The establishment of these military courts referred to in the Official Gazette of the army, the gazette also mentioned the establishment of the court in Zenica but not the one in Travnik. Is this perhaps a mistake you have made, or can you confirm that there was a military court in Travnik? In Article 5 of the text signed by Mr. Izetbegovic, it states that the military districts of the courts are in Banja Luka, Bihac, Mostar, Sarajevo, Tuzla, and Zenica. But Travnik isn't mentioned. What could you tell the Trial Chamber in order to clarify this?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have reliable information. Most probably the district military court in Travnik was established somewhat later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Another question for you, sir, in your capacity as a prosecutor, you were authorised to order investigations to be carried out. Who would be issued with that order? I'm not talking about the investigative judges; I'm talking about investigators themselves. Who did investigators belong to? Which body did those persons who conducted the investigations belong to?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that period of time, up to the 1st of August 2003, based on the request of the conducting investigation, the investigations were conducted by the investigative judge of the cantonal court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But when you were the one to issue an investigation to be carried out, and if you didn't issue that order to the investigative judge, who was it who went to the site? It was not the judge or yourself who went there; this was probably police officers. Who were they?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were authorised personnel of the public security centre, currently the MUP of the ZB canton who were charged with certain investigative operations before the official request for investigation was filed. They were sent to the site in order to verify information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it was the public security centre in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, in the district.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. In your capacity as a prosecutor, did you have any contacts with other bodies of authority, civilian or military, or were you in your office all the time and you didn't see anybody?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no way for me not to see people. I was in contact, because of the food, with the president of the municipality. It was a matter of survival. I had to ask for a paper, for carbon paper. We had old typewriters. There was no electricity. So most of my contacts were with the president of the municipality to provide for the survival of the prosecution and the survival of the court, because the court cannot work out the prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now just to clarify another thing, did you have any contact with the military authorities at the time?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the military authorities, I virtually had no contacts with them, no contacts at all. Yesterday, I testified that the Security Services Centre and the authorised personnel of that centre cooperated with the military; to be more specific, with the military police. Whenever necessary through the Security Services Centre, we cooperated with the military police. But it was via them, never directly, or at least I can't remember such cooperation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am turning to the Prosecution to see whether they have any re-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have just a couple of questions. And they relate to Exhibit DH56. And I would ask that that be document be returned to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this exhibit is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, if you could please turn to page 4 of that document and look again at the table listing the various statistics as set forth in the three columns, yesterday, the Presiding Judge asked you about the numbers on the far left. That is, the numbers 1 through 18. It's not clear from the transcript what those numbers refer to. Do you have any recollection what the numbers 1 through 18 on the left margin of DH56 for identification refers to?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can just interpret what I see in front of me. 212, 212 adults; 43 minors, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps, Witness, my question isn't clear. I'm looking at the numbers on the far left margin that are numbered 1 through 18. What do the numbers 1 through 18 refer to?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a certain order of data, an order of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: How is the information ordered? That's my question. What data or what order of information does this -- these numbers 1 through 18 refer to?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever has been entered was entered by the person who entered the information. The statistical data that were obtained were put in a systematic order in this particular way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have already put that question to you, and you didn't answer me. The Prosecution is putting this same question to you again. You're a professional. You must have an explanation with regard to the sequence and the classification. Do these numbers in a certain way correspond to certain crimes that were committed? You should be in the position to know the answer to this question. Yesterday, you didn't answer this question, and the Prosecution is now in a position to ask this question again. Maybe you don't know what these numbers represent. Maybe the Defence will provide us with an explanation. Maybe they can assist us in that respect because the Defence used to be a prosecutor at one time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to draw your attention to page 3, the last paragraph in which it says that the data was given according to the methodology requested by the republican prosecutor's office. I do not want to testify before this Trial Chamber, but given the experience that we have had, every year a higher prosecutor's office requests certain information from a lower prosecutor's office. And these data can be found in the records, and that is the number of criminal reports filed, the number of perpetrators, the number of requests for investigations, the number of persons who were charged, that is, indictments brought, the number of persons who were charged, and the number of suspects. I am not saying that all that I have just said corresponds entirely with the table we have in front of you, however, the Defence may try and find the methodology which was in place in 1993. We can provide it to the Trial Chamber so as to give a proper explanation to all of these figures. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. But maybe the witness could provide us with an answer. Sir, you must have sent such reports a number of times, so you must know what this is all about. Can you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the explanation that we have heard is good enough, and there is nothing else that I could add to the explanation. This is just an administrative matter, and I was not very familiar with that. It was Mr. Dzemaludin Mutapcic who was involved in that, and I'm really not in a position to provide you with any additional explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kapetanovic. The Prosecution has no further questions. And Mr. President, we would have no objection to DH56 being admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document was on stand by, still is on stand by. The decision is still pending. This document is now going to be given a number, DH56 for B/C/S version, and DH56/E for the English version. Mr. Kapetanovic, the Trial Chamber would like to thank you for coming to The Hague and answering the questions put to you both by the Prosecution and the Defence, as well as the questions put to you by the Judges. Thank you for staying here for two days. We wish you a happy return home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I am leaving this place with wonderful impressions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a new witness who should testify in keeping with Rule 92 bis. The Trial Chamber understands that the Prosecution is not going to examine the witness, that the statement of this witness will be introduced into the file. The witness will be cross-examined. However, may I ask the usher to go and bring the witness into the courtroom. Can we hear from the Prosecution whether there is an application for protective measures, Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, as Defence has already been informed about, we will make an oral application for protective measures for the next witness. And for that purpose, I would like to go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we need to raise the blinds.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are now in open session. The Trial Chamber has been informed that the Prosecution intends to have witnesses testifying by having recourse to the videoconference system. If that is the case, the Defence should inform me of any comments it has about this matter as soon as possible so that the Trial Chamber can render a decision on Friday at the latest. At this point in time, could the Prosecution tell us how many witnesses will be testifying via videolink, and could they inform us of the reasons for requesting that the witnesses testify in this manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, for that purpose, can we please go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll go back into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 4th day of March, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.56 p.m.,
